# Asset tools

The asset database, import and download, materials, textures, prefabs, audio generation and previews.

22 tools in the `asset` category. Badges: **read-only** tools never change the project; **mutating** tools are undoable and attributed; **open-world** tools reach outside the engine and MCP clients ask before running them.

| Tool | Summary |
|---|---|
| [`asset_import_mesh`](#asset_import_mesh) | Import a mesh (.obj, .glb, .gltf — e.g. |
| [`asset_request`](#asset_request) | Queue a request for generated content — kind: mesh (3D model), texture, sprite (2D), audio (sfx), music, video — with a prompt. |
| [`asset_requests`](#asset_requests) | List generated-asset requests and their status. |
| [`asset_complete`](#asset_complete) | Mark a request done with the generated file (project-relative). |
| [`asset_list`](#asset_list) | Search the project's assets (meshes, textures, materials, prefabs, scenes, audio...) by type, tag or text (matches path, description and tags; supports * globs). |
| [`asset_info`](#asset_info) | Everything about one asset: GUID, type, tags, description, provenance, import settings, which entities use it, and type-specific data (material fields, prefab contents). |
| [`asset_preview`](#asset_preview) | Render an isolated preview image of a mesh, material (on a sphere), texture or prefab — look before you place it. |
| [`asset_import`](#asset_import) | Register a file placed in the project (e.g. |
| [`asset_tag`](#asset_tag) | Set an asset's tags and/or description (and provenance). |
| [`asset_move`](#asset_move) | Rename or move an asset file (its .meta and GUID move with it) and update every reference in the open scene. |
| [`asset_refresh`](#asset_refresh) | Rescan the project folder for new or changed files (the editor also does this automatically). |
| [`material_create`](#material_create) | Create a reusable material asset (*.mat.json): color, metallic, roughness, emissive (glows with bloom), albedo texture with tiling, unlit. |
| [`material_update`](#material_update) | Change fields of an existing material; every entity using it updates instantly. |
| [`texture_generate`](#texture_generate) | Procedurally generate a seamless PBR texture set — albedo, normal map and ORM (occlusion/roughness/metallic) — for realistic or stylized surfaces: bricks, planks, cobblestone, rock, rust, marble, fabric, scales, ... |
| [`material_assign`](#material_assign) | Use a material asset on one or more entities (sets mesh.material; empty string clears it). |
| [`prefab_create`](#prefab_create) | Save an entity and all its children (components, behaviors, vars, tags) as a reusable prefab asset. |
| [`prefab_instantiate`](#prefab_instantiate) | Create an instance of a prefab. |

| [`sprite_sheet_slice`](#sprite_sheet_slice) | Describe a grid sprite sheet as an atlas (*.atlas.json) so frames get names: give the cell size (or columns/rows), optional margin/spacing, and either names or a prefix. |
| [`audio_generate`](#audio_generate) | Create a sound effect, ambience loop or piece of music as a WAV file in the project, procedurally and deterministically (the same seed and parameters always give the same audio) - no external generator needed. |
| [`audio_info`](#audio_info) | Measure an audio file (wav, mp3, flac): duration, sample rate, channels, peak and RMS in dBFS, integrated loudness (LUFS), clipping, DC offset, silence ratio, whether it starts or ends abruptly (clicks), and for loops how big the jump is at the loop point. |
| [`groom_export`](#groom_export) | Write a groom's rest-pose strands to a file for DCC round trips: .hair (Cem Yuksel's format, read by many hair tools), .groom.json (readable) or .skygroom (compact binary). |

### `asset_import_mesh` { #asset_import_mesh }

**Import mesh** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Import a mesh (.obj, .glb, .gltf — e.g. output of a 3D-generation model) and optionally assign it to an entity (its mesh becomes "asset:<path>"). Meshes are normalized to fit a 1m cube; glTF materials become a material asset. See also asset_import.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | Project-relative .obj/.glb/.gltf path |  |
| `entity` | integer \| string |  | Entity to assign the mesh to |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    asset_import_mesh {"path": "models/lantern.obj", "entity": "Lantern"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call asset_import_mesh '{"path": "models/lantern.obj", "entity": "Lantern"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "asset_import_mesh",
        "arguments": {
          "path": "models/lantern.obj",
          "entity": "Lantern"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `asset_request` { #asset_request }

**Request generated asset** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Queue a request for generated content — kind: mesh (3D model), texture, sprite (2D), audio (sfx), music, video — with a prompt. A connected generator (image/3D/audio model) or an agent fulfills it with asset_complete; results are applied to `target` automatically.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | yes | Asset kind | `mesh` `texture` `sprite` `audio` `music` `video` |
| `prompt` | string | yes | What to generate, in detail |  |
| `style` | string |  | Optional style guide, e.g. "low-poly pastel" |  |
| `target` | integer \| string |  | Entity that should receive the result |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    asset_request {"kind": "texture", "prompt": "weathered teak planks, seamless", "style": "photoreal", "target": "Deck"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call asset_request '{"kind": "texture", "prompt": "weathered teak planks, seamless", "style": "photoreal", "target": "Deck"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "asset_request",
        "arguments": {
          "kind": "texture",
          "prompt": "weathered teak planks, seamless",
          "style": "photoreal",
          "target": "Deck"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `asset_complete` { #asset_complete }

**Complete asset request** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Mark a request done with the generated file (project-relative). mesh -> imported and assigned to the target; texture -> set as the target's texture; sprite -> target becomes a camera-facing textured quad.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | yes | Request id |  |
| `path` | string |  | Generated file path |  |
| `failed` | boolean |  | Mark as failed instead |  |

### `asset_import` { #asset_import }

**Import asset** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Register a file placed in the project (e.g. by a generator) as an asset. Meshes (.glb/.gltf/.obj/.ply/.stl) are imported — glTF / OBJ+MTL materials become material assets, PLY/OBJ vertex colors are kept — and can be placed as a new entity right away. Rigged / animated glTF characters also get an animation library (<name>.anim: skeleton + clips) and a prefab with an animator, keep their real size (unless normalize is given) and are turned to face -Z; then use animation_list / animator_setup. Animation-only glTF files become clip libraries. To fetch models from the web use asset_download.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | Project-relative file path |  |
| `create_entity` | string |  | If set, create an entity with this name using the mesh |  |
| `position` | number[3] |  | Position for the created entity |  |
| `description` | string |  | What the asset is (helps future searches) |  |
| `tags` | string[] |  | Tags |  |
| `normalize` | boolean |  | Scale meshes to fit 1 m (default true; rigged characters default to their real size); false keeps real-world units |  |
| `z_up` | boolean |  | The mesh is Z-up (CAD, scans, some exporters) — rotate to Y-up |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    asset_import {"path": "characters/knight.glb", "create_entity": "Knight", "position": [0, 0, 0]}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call asset_import '{"path": "characters/knight.glb", "create_entity": "Knight", "position": [0, 0, 0]}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "asset_import",
        "arguments": {
          "path": "characters/knight.glb",
          "create_entity": "Knight",
          "position": [
            0,
            0,
            0
          ]
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `material_create` { #material_create }

**Create material** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Create a reusable material asset (*.mat.json): color, metallic, roughness, emissive (glows with bloom), albedo texture with tiling, unlit. Assign it with material_assign.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | color |  | Base color (multiplied with the texture) — hex string "#rrggbb[aa]" or [r,g,b(,a)] in 0..1 |  |
| `metallic` | number |  | 0 = dielectric, 1 = metal | 0 .. 1 |
| `roughness` | number |  | 0 = mirror, 1 = matte | 0.02 .. 1 |
| `emissive` | color |  | Emitted light; alpha is strength (glows with bloom) — hex string "#rrggbb[aa]" or [r,g,b(,a)] in 0..1 |  |
| `texture` | string |  | Albedo texture path (png/jpg), project-relative |  |
| `tilingU` | number |  | Texture repeats along U | 0.01 .. 1000 |
| `tilingV` | number |  | Texture repeats along V | 0.01 .. 1000 |
| `unlit` | boolean |  | Ignore lighting (flat look for 2D / UI / stylized) |  |
| `shading` | string |  | pbr = physically based, toon = cel bands + crisp highlights, unlit = flat, water = animated waves | `pbr` `toon` `unlit` `water` |
| `normalMap` | string |  | Normal map (png), project-relative |  |
| `ormMap` | string |  | Occlusion/roughness/metallic map (R/G/B), project-relative |  |
| `emissiveMap` | string |  | Emission map, multiplied with emissive |  |
| `normalStrength` | number |  | Normal map strength | 0 .. 4 |
| `triplanar` | boolean |  | World-space texture projection (tiling = repeats per meter) |  |
| `clearcoat` | number |  | Glossy lacquer layer (car paint, varnish) | 0 .. 1 |
| `subsurface` | number |  | Light bleeding through (skin, leaves, wax, snow) | 0 .. 1 |
| `rim` | number |  | Stylized rim light | 0 .. 4 |
| `outline` | number |  | Cartoon outline width in pixels | 0 .. 12 |
| `outlineColor` | color |  | Outline color — hex string "#rrggbb[aa]" or [r,g,b(,a)] in 0..1 |  |
| `doubleSided` | boolean |  | Render both faces |  |
| `occlusionStrength` | number |  | Ambient occlusion from the ORM map's red channel | 0 .. 1 |
| `alphaCutoff` | number |  | Alpha-tested cutout threshold (foliage, sails, fences); 0 = off | 0 .. 1 |
| `path` | string | yes | Project-relative path ending in .mat.json, e.g. materials/stone.mat.json |  |
| `preset` | string |  | Start from a built-in material (other fields override it) | `gold` `silver` `copper` `chrome` `brushed_steel` `iron` `plastic` `rubber` `ceramic` `car_paint` `glass` `water` `ice` `skin` `wax` `leaves` `snow` `velvet` `neon` `toon` `toon_metal` `clay` |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    material_create {"path": "materials/brass.mat.json", "preset": "gold", "roughness": 0.35, "color": "#c9a24a"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call material_create '{"path": "materials/brass.mat.json", "preset": "gold", "roughness": 0.35, "color": "#c9a24a"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "material_create",
        "arguments": {
          "path": "materials/brass.mat.json",
          "preset": "gold",
          "roughness": 0.35,
          "color": "#c9a24a"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `texture_generate` { #texture_generate }

**Generate PBR texture** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Procedurally generate a seamless PBR texture set — albedo, normal map and ORM (occlusion/roughness/metallic) — for realistic or stylized surfaces: bricks, planks, cobblestone, rock, rust, marble, fabric, scales, ... With create_material it also writes a ready material (triplanar by default, so it works on scaled primitives without stretching). Colors override the kind's defaults. The soft kinds `glow` (radial) and `curtain` (vertical rays fading upward) have transparent edges and make self-lit effect materials: particles, light pools, fake reflections, auroras, light shafts, steam.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | yes | Pattern | `noise` `marble` `wood` `planks` `bricks` `tiles` `cobblestone` `grass` `dirt` `sand` `rock` `metal_brushed` `rust` `fabric` `checker` `stripes` `hexagons` `scales` `stylized` `glow` `curtain` |
| `name` | string | yes | Base path without extension, e.g. textures/old_bricks |  |
| `size` | integer |  | Pixels, power of two 64..2048 (default 512) |  |
| `seed` | integer |  | Variation seed (default 1) |  |
| `scale` | number |  | Feature count across the tile (kind default if omitted) |  |
| `color1` | string |  | Primary color #rrggbb |  |
| `color2` | string |  | Secondary color #rrggbb |  |
| `color3` | string |  | Accent color (mortar, grout, veins, rust) #rrggbb |  |
| `roughness` | number |  | Base roughness 0..1 |  |
| `metallic` | number |  | Metallic 0..1 |  |
| `variation` | number |  | Color / height variation 0..1 |  |
| `bump` | number |  | Normal strength (default 1) |  |
| `create_material` | boolean |  | Also create materials/&lt;name&gt;.mat.json using the maps (default true) |  |
| `tiling` | number |  | Material repeats per meter (triplanar) — default 0.5 |  |
| `glow` | number |  | Emission strength for the soft effect kinds glow / curtain (default 1.5) |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    texture_generate {"kind": "cobblestone", "name": "street", "create_material": true, "tiling": 2}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call texture_generate '{"kind": "cobblestone", "name": "street", "create_material": true, "tiling": 2}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "texture_generate",
        "arguments": {
    ```

### `sprite_atlas_pack` { #sprite_atlas_pack }

**Pack sprite atlas** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Pack many images (a folder, a list, or globs like "sprites/hero/*.png") into one atlas texture plus a *.atlas.json describing every frame (trimmed of transparent borders, padded and edge-extruded so nothing bleeds). Frames are named after their files and keep natural order (run_2 before run_10). Sprites then use {"texture": "<atlas>.atlas.json", "frame": "run_3"}; the result suggests sprite_anim clips from numbered names (run_0..run_7 -> "run"). Example: {"folder": "art/hero", "output": "art/hero.atlas.json"}

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `folder` | string |  | Folder of images (non-recursive) |  |
| `inputs` | string[] |  | Image paths or globs (project-relative) |  |
| `output` | string |  | Atlas JSON path (default: &lt;folder&gt;.atlas.json) |  |
| `padding` | integer |  | Pixels between frames (default 2) |  |
| `trim` | boolean |  | Trim transparent borders (default true) |  |
| `extrude` | integer |  | Edge pixels repeated into the padding (default 1) |  |
| `max_size` | integer |  | Maximum atlas size (default 4096) |  |
| `power_of_two` | boolean |  | Power-of-two atlas size |  |
| `fps` | number |  | Frame rate for suggested clips (default 10) |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    sprite_atlas_pack {"folder": "art/hero", "output": "art/hero.atlas.json"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call sprite_atlas_pack '{"folder": "art/hero", "output": "art/hero.atlas.json"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "sprite_atlas_pack",
        "arguments": {
          "folder": "art/hero",
          "output": "art/hero.atlas.json"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `sprite_sheet_slice` { #sprite_sheet_slice }

**Slice sprite sheet** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Describe a grid sprite sheet as an atlas (*.atlas.json) so frames get names: give the cell size (or columns/rows), optional margin/spacing, and either names or a prefix. `animations` turns rows (or index ranges) into sprite_anim clips, and `entity` applies the sprite and its animations to an entity in one step. Example: {"image": "art/knight.png", "cell": [32, 32], "animations": {"idle": {"row": 0, "fps": 6}, "run": {"row": 1, "fps": 12}, "attack": {"frames": "16-21", "fps": 14, "loop": false}}, "entity": "Knight"}

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | string | yes | Sheet image (project-relative) |  |
| `cell` | integer[] |  | Cell size [w, h] in pixels |  |
| `columns` | integer |  | Columns (instead of cell) |  |
| `rows` | integer |  | Rows (instead of cell) |  |
| `margin` | integer |  | Border around the grid (pixels) |  |
| `spacing` | integer |  | Gap between cells (pixels) |  |
| `prefix` | string |  | Frame name prefix (default: image name + "_") |  |
| `names` | string[] |  | Frame names in order (left-&gt;right, top-&gt;bottom) |  |
| `skip_empty` | boolean |  | Drop fully transparent cells (default true) |  |
| `output` | string |  | Atlas path (default: &lt;image&gt;.atlas.json) |  |
| `animations` | object |  | clip -&gt; {row \| frames, fps, loop, events} |  |
| `entity` | integer \| string |  | Apply: sprite (atlas) + sprite_anim (clips) on this entity |  |
| `pixels_per_unit` | number |  | With entity: sprite pixelsPerUnit (default: cell height, i.e. 1 cell = 1 unit) |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    sprite_sheet_slice {"image": "art/knight.png", "cell": [32, 32], "animations": {"idle": {"row": 0, "fps": 6}, "run": {"row": 1, "fps": 12}, "attack": {"frames": "16-21", "fps": 14, "loop": false}}, "entity": "Knight"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call sprite_sheet_slice '{"image": "art/knight.png", "cell": [32, 32], "animations": {"idle": {"row": 0, "fps": 6}, "run": {"row": 1, "fps": 12}, "attack": {"frames": "16-21", "fps": 14, "loop": false}}, "entity": "Knight"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "sprite_sheet_slice",
        "arguments": {
          "image": "art/knight.png",
          "cell": [
            32,
            32
          ],
          "animations": {
            "idle": {
              "row": 0,
              "fps": 6
            },
            "run": {
              "row": 1,
              "fps": 12
            },
            "attack": {
              "frames": "16-21",
              "fps": 14,
              "loop": false
            }
          },
          "entity": "Knight"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `audio_generate` { #audio_generate }

**Generate sound or music** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Create a sound effect, ambience loop or piece of music as a WAV file in the project, procedurally and deterministically (the same seed and parameters always give the same audio) - no external generator needed. Presets: jump, coin, pickup, hit, explosion, laser, powerup, footstep_grass, footstep_stone, footstep_wood, door, ui_click, ui_hover, error, swoosh, shoot, wind_loop, rain_loop, fire_crackle_loop, ocean_waves_loop, ambient_drone, heartbeat. Names ending in _loop loop seamlessly (use them for ambience; set loop on the audio component). Use `seed` and `variations` for natural variety (footsteps!). Customize a preset with `pitch` (multiplier) and `volume`, or fully with `params`: layers of oscillators/noise with pitch slides, arpeggios, envelopes, filters and echo/reverb (call with list=true for the parameter reference). Music: pass `music` {mood: calm, happy, sad, tense, epic, mysterious, eerie, adventure, battle; tempo, key like "A minor", progression like "i VI III VII", bars, energy 0..1, reverb, and pad/bass/arp/melody/drums on/off}; it loops seamlessly. Pass `entity` to create or update that entity's audio component with the clip (loops, bus and spatial settings are chosen from the kind). The result includes loudness stats; check them with audio_info and audition with audio_play. Examples: {"preset":"jump","path":"audio/jump.wav"}; {"preset":"footstep_stone","variations":4}; {"music":{"mood":"epic","tempo":110,"bars":16},"path":"audio/theme.wav"}.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `preset` | string |  | Sound effect preset | `jump` `coin` `pickup` `hit` `explosion` `laser` `powerup` `footstep_grass` `footstep_stone` `footstep_wood` `door` `ui_click` `ui_hover` `error` `swoosh` `shoot` `wind_loop` `rain_loop` `fire_crackle_loop` `ocean_waves_loop` `ambient_drone` `heartbeat` |
| `params` | object |  | Custom sound parameters (see list=true): {layers:[{wave, freq, slide, attack, decay, lowpass, ...}], echo, reverb, volume, loopSeconds}. With a preset, these replace the preset's matching fields. |  |
| `music` | object |  | Generate music instead: {mood, tempo, key, progression, bars, energy, reverb, pad, bass, arp, melody, drums} |  |
| `path` | string |  | Output path, e.g. audio/jump.wav (default audio/&lt;name&gt;_&lt;seed&gt;.wav) |  |
| `seed` | integer |  | Variation seed (default 1) |  |
| `variations` | integer |  | Generate N variants with seeds seed..seed+N-1 (sfx only, 1..16, default 1); files get _1, _2 ... suffixes |  |
| `pitch` | number |  | Multiplier on the pitch of the preset's tonal layers (e.g. 0.5 = an octave lower) |  |
| `volume` | number |  | Output gain 0..4 (default 1; the sound is normalized to 0.9 peak first) |  |
| `entity` | integer \| string |  | Create/update this entity's audio component with the clip |  |
| `description` | string |  | What the sound is (stored with the asset) |  |
| `tags` | string[] |  | Asset tags |  |
| `list` | boolean |  | Only list presets, moods and the parameter reference; generate nothing |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    audio_generate {"preset": "jump", "path": "audio/jump.wav"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call audio_generate '{"preset": "jump", "path": "audio/jump.wav"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "audio_generate",
        "arguments": {
          "preset": "jump",
          "path": "audio/jump.wav"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `audio_info` { #audio_info }

**Analyze audio** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--ro" title="Never changes the scene">read-only</span>

Measure an audio file (wav, mp3, flac): duration, sample rate, channels, peak and RMS in dBFS, integrated loudness (LUFS), clipping, DC offset, silence ratio, whether it starts or ends abruptly (clicks), and for loops how big the jump is at the loop point. Returns warnings (clipping, too quiet/loud, click risks, loop seam) and the asset's provenance. Use it to verify generated audio since you cannot listen: sound effects around -23 to -14 LUFS, music around -20 to -16, ambience quieter. Example: {"path":"audio/jump.wav"}.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | Project-relative audio file |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    audio_info {"path": "audio/jump.wav"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call audio_info '{"path": "audio/jump.wav"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "audio_info",
        "arguments": {
          "path": "audio/jump.wav"
        }
      }
    }
    ```
